2026-09-23T09:11:05.754244+00:00

- No duplication of data, if same part numbers are mentiend with same qty and price, properly deduplicate that 
- Different attachment may contain same quotation
- If same quotation is present in multiple attachments, then combine the data from all the attachments and return a single quotation object.
- For each distinct quotation, extract the full set of fields described in the per-quotation schema below.
- Return a single top-level JSON object with the key ``quotations`` whose value is a JSON array. Each element of the array is one fully-populated quotation object using the schema below. If only one quotation is present, return an array with a single element. If no quotation can be extracted, return ``{"quotations": []}``.

**How to decide what counts as a distinct quotation:**
- A unique ``quote_number`` almost always indicates a distinct quotation. Different ``quote_number`` values MUST become separate elements in the ``quotations`` array.
- Different attachments that each look like a complete standalone quotation (their own header, supplier block, line items, totals) MUST become separate elements even if the ``quote_number`` is missing.
- Do NOT split a single quotation into multiple elements just because its line items span multiple pages or sheets.

  "quote_expiry_date": "The expiration date of the quotation, in ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD) as string",
  "shipping_and_delivery": {
    "shipping_instructions": {
      "delivery_method": "The delivery method mentioned, e.g., standard, express, courier as string",
      "special_handling": "Any special handling instructions such as fragile, temperature-controlled, hazardous as string",
      "insurance": "Whether insurance is required/optional/none as stated in the quotation as string"

    "shipping_method": "The primary shipping method used, e.g., Air, Sea, Road, Courier. Mandatory field as string",
    "delivery_location": "The final delivery location or warehouse specified in the quotation as string",
    "bill_to_address": {
      "street": "Street portion of the consignee's address as string",
      "city": "City of consignee's address as string",
      "state": "State/Province/Region of consignee's address as string",
      "zipcode": "Postal code as string",
      "country": "3-letter ISO ALPHA-3 country code, e.g., IND for India"
    },
    "ship_to_address": {
      "street": "Street portion of the consignee's address as string",
      "city": "City of consignee's address as string",
      "state": "State/Province/Region of consignee's address as string",
      "zipcode": "Postal code as string",
      "country": "3-letter ISO ALPHA-3 country code, e.g., IND for India as string"
    }
  },
  "supplier_information": {
    "supplier_name": "The name of the supplier issuing the quotation as string",
    "supplier_email": "email of supplier in the document else none as string"
    "address": "The supplier's full address in a single line as string",
    "contact": "Primary phone number of supplier contact person, if provided as string",
    "website": "Supplier's website URL, if available as string"

  "currency": "The currency used in the quotation as ISO 4217 code, e.g., USD as string",

Map common phrases to the standard code (e.g. 'Delivered Duty Paid'→DDP, 'Free on Board'→FOB). If no valid Incoterm is found, use null.]",
  "buyer": {
    "name": "Name of the consignee company receiving the goods, must be $consignee_company as string",

      "manufacturer_part_number": "Extract manufacturer part number from 'PART:', 'MFG P/N:', or next to manufacturer name. Do not create on your own. If none available, default to description. as string",

      "notes": "[Any additional comments specific to the line item as list of str, such as Discount mentioned on this part]",
      "certifications": "[Certifications for this line item. Use standard names: ISO 9001, RoHS, REACH, CE, UL, CSA, etc. Normalize variants to standard abbreviations. As list of strings; use null or [] if none.]",

  "quotations": [
